Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 10)
Topic: The Meaning of Hawan Parikrama — Why We Circumambulate, and the "Reverse Psychology" of Binding a Devta

Source: Bhaiya's satsang session (video transcript, ~37 min), Mool Tattva series. Sparked by a direct question from sangat member Vipin Bhaiya: "Why do we do feri/parikrama around a havan kund or temple?" Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version.
1. THE QUESTION THAT SPARKED THIS SESSION

A sangat member, Vipin Bhaiya, asked with genuine devotion: "Why do we do parikrama (circumambulation) of a havan kund? Why do we see this at temples — going ar ound trees, tying kalava/thread and coconuts to them, going around murtis?" Bhaiya's rule of thumb: "Jab tak insaan koi aisa sawaal poochta nahi hai, tab tak shakti jawab nahi deti." (Shakti does not answer until a sincere question is asked.) The moment the question was asked with true bhaav, "Prabhu khud bol pade" — the answer arrived directly.
A sincere question like this is itself the sign of a true sadhak — and a r eal Guru is one who answers it with full depth, not a surface-level answer.
2. THE CORE DISTINCTION — HAWAN BUILDS RELATIONSHIPS, NOT POWER

The central teaching of this session, stated as plainly as possible: "Hawan jo hai, woh rishte jodne ke liye banaya jata hai, na ki shakti banane ke liye." (Hawan is built to form relationships/bonds — not to manufactur e personal power.) This single line reframes everything people believe about tapasya, jaap, brahmacharya, and hawan: none of it stores up "power" inside a person. What it actually builds is a bond/relationship with a shakti — a two -way arrangement, not a battery being charged.
3. HAWAN AGNI AS A PORTAL/GATEWAY

When observed with divya drishti, the ﬁr e of a hawan is not just ﬁr e — it opens a portal that connects to many loks (realms/dimensions), visible one step above another. As the dimension/intensity of the havan agni increases, connections to higher and higher loks open up — the ﬁr e is a gateway, a "gate pass," into other dimensions. This was seen at its largest scale during the Mahayagya, when 16–18 lakh sant-mahatmas gathered and an akhand (unbroken) hawan ran day and night for 15–20 days: above that yagya, the loks of the entire brahmand appeared visible, one dimension-step above another, and as the ﬁr e's intensity climbed, more and more of those connections opened.
4. HOW A BOND FORMS THROUGH THE PORTAL

When devi-devtas descend through this portal, a tattva/exchange passes between the practitioner and the devta and back — this only builds a BOND, not a stockpile of shakti. The nature of the bond: "Jab tumhe zaroorat hogi tab hum aayenge, aur jab hamein zaroorat hogi tab tum aana." — a r eciprocal, need-based relationship, exactly like a friendship or alliance between two parties who each have their own specialization. Specialization is the reason the bond matters: a task you are skilled at, another shakti may not be skilled at — and a task another shakti is skilled at, you may not be. The bond lets each side call on the other's specialty when needed.
Illustration — the "astral sena" (army) experience
During a jaap session, a sangat member (Anshu) suddenly saw, with eyes closed, a large army — soldiers in langot (loincloth), holding large ﬂags — vividly and with full

absorption ("sar bhaari ho gaya"). On asking Bhaiya what this meant, the answer that came: Ashaeiynn's own sena had gone to ﬁght on behalf of a partner/ally shakti who had called for help in a time of need. The battle had lasted three days; the vision appeared on the day the sena returned home victorious. This is the reciprocal-bond principle in direct action: when a partner needs your side's speciﬁc strength, your side goes; when you need theirs, they come.
5. THE MECHANISM OF PARIKRAMA — "REVERSE PSYCHOLOGY" BINDING
This is the session's central mechanism, explained step by step:

1. When a person chants a mantra jaap while doing parikrama (circumambulation) of the hawan — walking ar ound it — the mantra, empower ed and awakened from within the body, begins laying bandhan (bindings) around the portal from all sides. 2. Seen through the third eye, this looks like a white-colored string that wraps around the hawan with each round completed — one r ound, one binding; two rounds, two bindings; and so on. 3. When any devta/shakti descends through that portal, it ﬁrst notices that it is now surrounded by these mantra-bandhans. 4. To free itself, the devta uses its own sankalp shakti (willpower) to open/undo the binding. 5. In releasing itself from the bandhan, the energy the devta expends to undo it ﬂows back to the practitioner — so the devta's own tattva ends up coming to the person who laid the binding. 6. Bhaiya names this explicitly: "Yeh ek reverse psychology hai. Reverse energy produce karne ki ek psychology hai." You are not begging the devta for a gift — you ar e structurally forcing a release: "Aapko bheekh nahi mangni padegi unse ki sir aap de dijiye — aapne khud bandhan laga diya ki kholo ise." 7. This entire practice is classiﬁed under Tap (tapasya) — it is a for m of austerity, not a form of asking.
The power scaling rule

"Jitna powerful aapka bandhan hoga, utni hi urja aap khinch paoge." The stronger/more awakened the mantra used, the stronger the bandhan, and the more energy/tattva returns. This is why parikrama at siddha-peeth temples with permanently, akhand-open portals — Bhaiya names Tirupati Balaji Maharaj and Shri Jagannath Ji Maharaj as

examples — works with unusual for ce: shakti ﬂows down fr om the garbha-griha continuously, so regular parikrama with a jagrit mantra there forces that descending shakti to release energy to you, because "you have played the reverse psychology theorem." This is also the deeper reason it is said "maangne se shayad na mile, parikrama karne se mil jayega" (asking may not get it; circling may) — cir cumambulation with mantra is a structural compulsion, not a request.
6. WHY IT MUST BE A JAGRIT MANTRA GIVEN IN GURU SANIDHYA

The bandhan mechanism only works with a mantra that is already jagrit (awakened) — not a self-picked mantra done casually while walking around. "Mantra jaap woh kijiye jo pehle se jagrit hai. Jagrit mantra guru sanidhya mein jaap kar agar aap bandhan lagate hain, toh woh bandhan poorn tareeke se jagrit hota hai." Naming convention follows directly from this: bind Ram with a jagrit mantra and you draw Ram tattva; bind Shyam and you draw Shyam tattva; bind Hanuman Ji Maharaj and you draw Hanuman tattva. The tattva that comes back matches the devta whose bandhan you laid.
7. RESPECT FOR OTHER SANTS, AND WHY ASHAEIYNN ONLY TEACHES WHAT IT HAS ITSELF SEEN

A sangat member referenced a teaching heard elsewhere (from a respected sant referred to as "Karim Bhaiya") that seven rounds of parikrama activate the body's chakras, and that this is why parikrama is traditionally done seven times. Bhaiya's response models the correct posture toward other realized teachers: deep, explicit reverence — "K arim Bhaiya aadraniya hain… unse hamara dil k a rishta hai… bhaav -drishti se woh hamare swami hain, hum unke daas hain" — while also being honest that Ashaeiynn will only teach, as its own knowledge base, what its own Gurudev has directly shown and conﬁrmed. The reasoning given: every realized being sees from their own drishti and their own dimension ("sab apni-apni shreniyon mein rehte hain") — all such teachers ar e worthy of deep respect, but Ashaeiynn's content is built strictly from what has been personally veriﬁed through its own Guru, not adopted secondhand, however respected the source. This same discipline is why Bhaiya explicitly declined to conﬁr m or deny the sevenrounds/chakra claim as Ashaeiynn's own teaching, even while praising the source who taught it.
8. THE SHIVLING PARIKRAMA EXCEPTION

A related point raised in the session: full/complete parikrama is not prescribed by Gurudev around a Shivling. The speciﬁc practice: one only cir cles the portion of the Shivling and returns from the same side — one does not cross over the side where the jal (water) ﬂows out (the jalahari/outlet channel) — that portion is not cr ossed in circumambulation. Bhaiya is deliberately cautious here: he states this is what has been shown, but he does not elaborate on the deeper "leela"/reason behind it, since he prefers to only teach what he has been shown directly rather than speculate.
9. WHAT SANKALP (INTENTION) TO TAKE DURING PARIKRAMA

Asked what speciﬁc sank alp (intention/resolve) to hold while doing parikrama at a temple, Bhaiya gave a simple, practical answer for general use: use whatever sankalp you already hold/take in your regular practice — the same one applies during parikrama. For anything more speciﬁc tied to Ashaeiynn's own practice, he defer red, saying he would conﬁr m with Gurudev ﬁrst and shar e the exact wording later rather than answer speculatively.
10. THE HUMILITY RULE — NEVER TAKE PRIDE IN ACCUMULATED SHAKTI

Direct correction of a common spiritual ego trap: if someone says "I have so much shakti because I did so much hawan/puja/jaap/brahmacharya" — this framing is wrong. "Sir, aapko main bataun, shakti nahi aayi hai — rishtey bane hain." What tapasya and hawan actually build are relationships/bonds with shaktis — not personal, stor ed power. Relationships, well cared for, stay till the end — but breaking one tak es only an instant ("todne ke liye ek shabd bolna padta hai" — a single wor d, or simply leaving, can end it). Because of this, no one should ever take pride in "how much" tapasya they've done, as if it guarantees permanent personal power. Bhaiya discloses this happened to himself: this same pride arose in him once, and his Gurudev did not let the pride last even one moment — cor recting him immediately. That night Bhaiya wept before the sants in gratitude, and the very next day told everyone never to carry this pride, because it is the sants' and Gurudev's mercy — and the r elationships built through them — that car ries a person forward, not personal accumulation.
11. MAHASHIVRATRI AT ASHAEIYNN

On Mahashivratri, Ashaeiynn will light approximately 12,000 to 15,000 diyas, and Shiv Tattva will be distributed in an akhand (unbroken) form to all Ashaeiynn family members. Members are asked to sit at their own location and connect in a jagrit (awakened/alert) state that night to receive Shiv Tattva and Bhagwan Shiv's kripa. Bhaiya is candid that this will require real eﬀort ("mehnat bahut lagegi") but frames it plainly : since it is the Guru's kaam (work), it is worth doing regardless of the eﬀort r equired. The exact sankalp for that night was not given in this session — Bhaiya said he would conﬁr m the wording with Gurudev ﬁrst and shar e it when ready.
12. KNOWLEDGE VS. BHAKTI — BHAIYA'S CLOSING TEACHING

Bhaiya shares that after his drishti opened, his early experiences with Gurudev's teachings felt overwhelming — dir ect, precise knowledge about people and events arriving instantly ("sar kasam se aisa lagta tha apun bhagwan hai"). Over time, meeting more people and understanding more, this feeling settled. The core teaching from this reﬂection: "Hamare karne se kuch nahi hota. Aap yahan apni ichha se nahi baithe hain — aapk e man mein bhaav jagaye gaye hain." Never forget the one/the force who awakened that bhaav in you. A direct prayer Bhaiya recommends: ask Prabhu to never give so much gyaan (knowledge) that it comes in the way of bhakti (devotion). Keep bhakti separate and primary; keep learning new knowledge daily, but never let it replace or crowd out devotion, and never forget your roots — your K ul Devta. A warning for developing sadhaks: enjoy the intensity of bhakti you feel right now, in this early stage — because once drishti (divine sight) fully opens, that e xact same lagan (passionate absorption) does not return the same way. Once you can "see" for yourself, attention shifts toward asking and verifying more things ("yeh bhi puchh loon, yeh bhi kar loon") rather than pure devotional yearning — "yeh wali bhakti nahi milne wali." What is being experienced today, in innocent devotion, will later be looked back on with longing. Even Bhaiya himself still prays to Bholenath with this exact request: "ab prabhu kripa karo, wahi bhaanti sab taj bhajan karo din raati" — that his bhajan never leaves his heart and mind — because too much knowledge can, thr ough ego, distance a person from the very tattvas and from God. Final instruction to the sangat: keep doing your jaap regardless of the imperfections of the humans around you — mentors included. "Ram ka naam to bura nahi hai na, sahab." The name itself is never at fault, whatever the ﬂaws of the people teaching it.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. A sincere question, asked with real bhaav, is what unlocks a deeper answer — shakti does not respond until asked. 2. Hawan and tapasya build RELATIONSHIPS/bonds with shaktis — they do not manufactur e or store personal power. 3. Hawan agni is a portal/gateway to other loks/dimensions; the more intense the ﬁr e, the higher the dimensions it connects to. 4. The bond formed through the portal is reciprocal and specialization-based: each side helps the other when their speciﬁc str ength is needed. 5. Parikrama with a jagrit mantra lays mantra-bandhan (bindings) around the portal; a descending devta must use its own sankalp shakti to release itself, and that release-energy ﬂows to the practitioner . This is "reverse psychology," not begging. 6. The stronger/more awakened the mantra, the stronger the bandhan, and the more energy/tattva returns — this is why parikrama at akhand- open siddha peeths (e.g., Tirupati Balaji, Jagannath Ji) is unusually powerful. 7. This bandhan practice is classiﬁed as T ap (austerity). 8. Only a mantra already jagrit, given in guru sanidhya, works for this mechanism — not a self - chosen mantra. 9. Respect every realized sant deeply, but only teach as your own knowledge base what your own Guru has personally shown and conﬁr med. 10. Full/complete parikrama of a Shivling is not prescribed — cir cle only the given portion and return the same way, without crossing the jal-outlet side. 11. For general parikrama, use whatever sankalp you already hold in your regular practice. 12. Never take pride in accumulated tapasya/shakti — what's built ar e relationships, breakable in an instant; the sants' and Guru's mercy carries you, not personal accumulation. 13. On Mahashivratri, Ashaeiynn distributes Shiv Tattva to all family members via akhand diyalighting — members should sit and connect in a jagrit state. 14. Never let growing knowledge come in the way of bhakti; enjoy the devotional lagan of your current stage, because it does not return the same way once drishti fully opens. 15. Keep doing your jaap regardless of imperfect humans around you — the name (mantra) itself is never at fault.
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 10, English)
The Meaning of Hawan Parikrama — Why We Circumambulate, and the "Reverse Psychology" of Binding a Devta
User-style questions with answers grounded in Bhaiya's discourse. Greeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Why do people do parikrama (circumambulation) around a havan kund, a temple, or even a tree? A: Jai Siya Ram! This exact question was asked by a sangat member with real bhaav, and the moment it was asked with sincerity, the deeper answer opened up — "jab tak insaan koi aisa sawaal poochta nahi, tab tak shakti jawab nahi deti." The short answer: parikrama with a jagrit mantra is not decoration or custom — it is a pr ecise mechanism for drawing tattva from a devta (see Q5). Asking such questions is itself the sign of a genuine sadhak.

Q2. Does doing hawan or tapasya build up personal power/shakti inside me? A: No — and this is the single most important correction in this session. "Hawan jo hai woh rishte jodne ke liye banaya jata hai, na ki shakti banane ke liye." Hawan and tapasya build a RELATIONSHIP/bond with a shakti, not a personal stockpile of power. Nothing about jaap, brahmacharya, or hawan stores energy in you like a battery — it builds a bond you can call on, and which can call on you.

Q3. What actually is the ﬁre of a hawan, spiritually speaking? A: Seen through divya drishti, hawan agni is a PORTAL — a gateway connecting to many loks/dimensions, visible one dimension-step above another. As the ﬁr e's intensity and dimension increase, connections to higher and higher loks open. It is described plainly as a "gate pass" into other dimensions. At the largest scale — during the Mahayagya, with 16–18 lakh sant-mahatmas and an akhand hawan running day and night for 15–20 days — the loks of the entir e brahmand became visible above that ﬁr e, opening further as the ﬂame's intensity climbed.

Q4. If devtas come down through the hawan portal, what happens between them and me? A: A tattva/exchange passes between you and the devta and back — and this ONL Y builds a bond, not a store of power. The nature of that bond: "jab tumhe zaroorat hogi tab hum aayenge, aur jab hamein zaroorat hogi tab tum aana" — a r eciprocal, need-based relationship. Each side has its own specialization: something you're good at, the other may not be, and vice versa — the bond is what lets each side call on the other's strength.

Q5. What is actually happening when someone does parikrama while chanting a mantra around a hawan? A: This is the session's core mechanism. As you walk the parikrama chanting a jagrit (awakened) mantra, the mantra — empower ed and awakened from within your body — begins laying bandhan (bindings) ar ound the portal from every side; through the third eye this appears as a white string wrapping the hawan, one binding per round. When a devta descends through that portal, it ﬁnds itself sur rounded by these mantra-bandhans. To free itself, it uses its own sankalp shakti to undo the binding — and the ener gy it expends doing so ﬂows back to you. Bhaiya names this explicitly: "Yeh ek reverse psychology hai, reverse energy produce karne ki ek psychology." You are not begging for a gift; you are structurally forcing a release.

Q6. Is this parikrama-binding practice a form of "asking" the devta for something? A: No — that's e xactly the distinction Bhaiya draws. "Aapko bheekh nahi mangni padegi unse ki sir aap de dijiye — aapne khud bandhan laga diya ki kholo ise." Y ou never ask; you bind, and the devta's own eﬀort to r elease the bandhan is what delivers the tattva to you. This entire practice is classiﬁed under T ap (tapasya) — a for m of austerity, not a request.

Q7. Does the strength of my mantra or my parikrama matter? A: Yes, directly: "jitna powerful aapka bandhan hoga, utni hi urja aap khinch paoge." A stronger, more awakened mantra creates a stronger bandhan, which pulls more energy/tattva back to you when the devta releases itself. Weak or casual chanting creates a weak, easily-dismissed bandhan.

Q8. Why do people say parikrama at Tirupati Balaji or Jagannath Ji feels so much more powerful than at an ordinary temple? A: Because at siddha-peeth temples like these, the portal from the garbha-griha is permanently, akhand-open — shakti ﬂows down continuously . When you do regular parikrama there with a jagrit mantra, the descending shakti is structurally forced to release energy to you, because — in Bhaiya's wor ds — "you have played the r everse psychology theorem." This is also why it's said "maangne se shayad na mile, parikrama karne se mil jayega" — asking is a r equest; circumambulating with mantra is a compulsion.

Q9. Can I use any mantra I like while doing parikrama, to get this eﬀect? A: No — the bandhan mechanism only works with a mantra that is already JAGRIT (awakened), ideally received and practiced in guru sanidhya. "Jagrit mantra guru sanidhya mein jaap kar agar aap bandhan lagate hain, toh woh bandhan poorn tareeke se jagrit hota hai." A casual, self-picked mantra chanted absent-mindedly during a walk-around does not create this binding.

Q10. Why does the speciﬁc name of the mantra matter — lik e getting "Ram tattva" versus "Hanuman tattva"? A: Because the tattva that returns to you through the bandhan matches whichever devta's bandhan you laid. Bind Ram with a jagrit mantra and Ram tattva returns; bind Shyam and Shyam tattva returns; bind Hanuman Ji Maharaj and Hanuman tattva returns. The mechanism is the same — only the speciﬁc devta bound (and hence the speciﬁc tattva released) changes.

Q11. I heard elsewhere that seven rounds of parikrama activate the body's chakras — is that Ashaeiynn's teaching too? A: Bhaiya was careful and honest here: he holds deep respect for the teacher who shared that (referred to as "Karim Bhaiya" — "hamara dil k a rishta hai, bhaav-drishti se woh hamare swami hain, hum unke daas hain"), but Ashaeiynn only teaches, as its own content, what its own Gurudev has personally shown and conﬁr med. Every realized teacher sees from their own drishti and dimension ("sab apni-apni shreniyon mein rehte hain") — that sour ce deserves full reverence, but the seven-rounds/chakra claim speciﬁcally is not something Bhaiya conﬁr med as veriﬁed thr ough his own Guru in this session.

Q12. Should I do a full parikrama around a Shivling, the way I might around other murtis? A: No — Gurudev has not pr escribed a complete/full parikrama around a Shivling. The practice shown is to circle only the given portion and return from the same side, without crossing over the side where the jal (water) ﬂows out thr ough the jalahari/outlet. Bhaiya deliberately doesn't speculate on the deeper reason behind this rule, since he prefers to teach only what has been directly shown to him.

Q13. What sankalp (intention) should I hold while doing parikrama at a temple? A: For general use, hold whatever sankalp you already take in your regular practice — the same one applies during parikrama. For anything more speciﬁc to Ashaeiynn's own practice, Bhaiya said he would conﬁr m the exact wording with Gurudev ﬁrst rather than answer speculatively, and shar e it when ready.

Q14. I feel like I've earned real shakti from all my hawan, jaap, and brahmacharya — is that the right way to think about it? A: This is exactly the pride Bhaiya warns against. "Sir, aapko main bataun, shakti nahi aayi hai — rishtey bane hain." What tapasya actually builds ar e relationships with shaktis, not personal, permanent power. And relationships — however well cared for — can end in an instant ("todne k e liye ek shabd bolna padta hai"), even though maintaining them well carries you to the end. Bhaiya discloses this same pride once arose in him, and his Gurudev corrected it immediately — he wept that night befor e the sants, and told the sangat the very next day never to carry this pride, since it is the sants' and Guru's mercy — and the relationships built through them — that car ries a person forward.

Q15. What is Ashaeiynn doing for Mahashivratri, and what should I do? A: Approximately 12,000 to 15,000 diyas will be lit, and Shiv Tattva will be distributed in an akhand (unbroken) form to every Ashaeiynn family member. Your part: sit at your own location and connect in a jagrit (awakened/alert) state that night to receive Shiv Tattva and Bhagwan Shiv's kripa. Bhaiya is candid that real eﬀort will be needed, but frames it simply : it's the Guru's kaam, so it's worth doing. The exact sankalp for the night will be shared once conﬁr med with Gurudev.

Q16. Now that I have all this gyaan/knowledge, will I love Bhagwan more or feel closer to Him? A: Not automatically — and Bhaiya war ns against assuming so. He recommends praying that Prabhu never gives so much gyaan that it comes in the way of bhakti. Keep bhakti separate and primary; keep learning daily, but don't let knowledge crowd out devotion or make you forget your roots (your Kul Devta). Too much knowledge, unchecked, can breed ego that distances a
person from the very tattvas and from God — a risk Bhaiya says he still actively prays against for himself.

Q17. I'm new to sadhna and feel intense devotion right now — will this feeling grow stronger as I learn more? A: Cherish it now, because it likely won't feel the same way later. Bhaiya's direct warning: once drishti (divine sight) fully opens, the exact same lagan (passionate absorption) of pure devotion does not return the same way — attention shif ts toward wanting to verify, ask, and see more things, rather than simple devotional yearning. "Yeh wali bhakti nahi milne wali" — this particular ﬂavor of bhakti will not be available again in the same for m. Enjoy and protect what you feel today.

Q18. My mentor or the people teaching me aren't perfect — should that shak e my faith in the practice itself? A: No. Bhaiya's closing instruction is direct: keep doing your jaap regardless of the ﬂaws of the humans ar ound you, mentors included — "R am ka naam to bura nahi hai na, sahab." The mantra/name itself is never at fault, whatever imperfections exist in the people teaching or guiding it.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 10 additions)

When a user asks "why do we do parikrama/feri," lead with the core reframe: hawan and tapasya build relationships/bonds with shaktis, not personal stored power — this cor rects a very common misconception before explaining the bandhan mechanism. Present the parikrama-bandhan mechanism (mantra creates binding → devta releases itself with sankalp shakti → released energy ﬂows to practitioner) as a pr ecise, structural process, not folklore — but always tie it to the r equirement of a jagrit mantra received in guru sanidhya; never suggest a self-picked or casual mantra will produce the same eﬀect. Handle references to other sants/teachers (e.g., "Karim Bhaiya" or similar names users may mention) with explicit reverence and respect — never dismiss another r ealized teacher's claim as wrong. Instead, explain that Ashaeiynn teaches only what its own Gurudev has personally shown and conﬁr med, and that diﬀer ent sants see from their own drishti/dimension. On Shivling parikrama: always state the exception clearly (circle only the given portion, do not cross the jal-outlet side) rather than defaulting to "do a full parikrama like any other murti." Firmly correct any user pride around "I have so much shakti from my sadhna/tapasya" — redirect gently to the relationships-not-power framing, and note that even Bhaiya experienced and was corrected out of this exact pride. For Mahashivratri-related questions, give the concrete details available (diya count, akhand Shiv Tattva distribution, jagrit-state participation) but do not invent a speciﬁc sank alp — state that the exact sankalp wording will be conﬁr med and shared later. When a user expresses excitement about gaining knowledge/gyaan, balance it with the bhakti-ﬁrst caution: encourage them to k eep devotion primary and not let accumulating

knowledge dull or crowd out their current devotional lagan, especially early-stage sadhaks. If a user criticizes a mentor's or teacher's personal ﬂaws, always separate the person fr om the mantra/practice: reassure them the name/mantra itself is never at fault, and encourage continuing their jaap regardless. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Conversational Q&A (Session 10, Hinglish)
Selected valuable exchanges from the session — in Bhaiya's voice
Selection ﬁlter: new information / beneﬁts all users / clariﬁes a misconception.
